panels.title: TCP SYN / RST / FIN over Time
panels.description: TCP control-packet counts per interval. RST tracking SYN means connections are being refused or torn down abnormally; FIN tracking SYN means they are closing cleanly. Needs fields added by the collector upgrade, so it stays empty for any part of the range recorded before that.

panels.title: Reset Ratio (RST / SYN)
panels.description: Resets as a percentage of connection attempts. A few percent is normal; sustained high values mean a service is refusing connections, or something is probing closed ports.

panels.title: Top Reset Conversations
panels.description: Conversations carrying TCP resets, most first. Repeated resets to the same service point at a dead or refusing listener; resets spread across many destinations look more like scanning.

panels.title: Connection Completion by Source
panels.description: SYN versus FIN per source. A source with many SYNs and few FINs is failing to complete connections — a scan, an unreachable service, or an aggressive retry loop. Note both counters are summed over ~5s flow fragments, so treat the percentage as a ratio, not an exact handshake count.

panels.title: Mean Packet Size over Time
panels.description: Average packet size across all flows. Small packets dominate interactive and control traffic; large packets mean bulk transfer.

panels.title: Packet Size Profile by Application
panels.description: Mean and max packet size per nDPI application, averaged across that application's flows. Separates chatty small-packet protocols (VoIP, gaming, control) from bulk movers running at the MTU.

list.name: site
list.label: Site
list.description: Which tzsp-monitor instance these panels read. Remote sites are the REMOTE_SITE_* lines in properties.yml of the instance serving this Grafana; each is a datasource pointed at that site's own InfluxDB, so nothing is copied between sites. Controls never follow this box: rule suppression and reverse DNS only ever act on the local site, and are inert while another site is selected.

list.name: cidr
list.label: CIDR filter
list.description: Restrict every panel to traffic with either endpoint in this range, e.g. 10.12.0.0/16, 10.12.6.0/24, or a bare IP. Leave empty for no filter. Prefix lengths other than /8, /16, /24 and /32 round down to the enclosing octet boundary, so /20 behaves as /16 and may show a wider range than typed.
